Classical frequentist methods assume fixed parameters, but sports data exhibit non-stationary patterns (e.g., injury dynamics). Bayesian inference updates priors via likelihood, offering recursive calibration. Conformal prediction provides finite-sample coverage guarantees without distributional assumptions, aligning with adversarial game theory. Failure modes include overfitting to recent form, ignoring latent variables, and adversarial manipulation of information flows. Cross-layer veto conditions require orthogonal feature spaces to prevent leakage between training/validation splits.
